class.name: NetwInterestBitSet
class.brief_description: Packed peer-bit rows, and the set operations [NetwInterestEngine] composes verdicts out of.
class.description: A row is a [PackedInt64Array] using bits [code]0[/code] through [code]62[/code] of each word. The sign bit is never touched, so every row stays a positive integer on both sides of the language boundary, where GDScript has no unsigned integer to receive one in. [codeblock] var row := PackedInt64Array() row = NetwInterestBitSet.with_bit(row, 3) NetwInterestBitSet.test(row, 3) # true NetwInterestBitSet.bits(row) # [3] [/codeblock] Every operation returns a new row rather than editing one in place, and a row is a bare [PackedInt64Array] rather than an object. Both are deliberate: rows are copied to worker tasks by value, and an object or a per-row wrapper is what would stop them. A shorter row is read as zero past its end, so operands of different widths compose without being resized first.

method.name: bits
method.description: Every set bit in [param row], ascending.

method.name: empty
method.description: A row with room for [param bit_count] bits and none of them set.

method.name: equals
method.description: Whether [param left] and [param right] hold the same bits, whatever their widths.

method.name: full
method.description: A row with every bit below [param bit_count] set.

method.name: intersect
method.description: The bits present in both [param left] and [param right].

method.name: popcount
method.description: How many bits [param row] has set.

method.name: resized
method.description: A copy of [param row] holding exactly [param words] words, every one of them written. Widening leaves the new words clear; narrowing drops whatever was above. Writing them is the contract rather than a detail: a packed array of a trivially constructible type does not value-initialise the words it grows by in every build, so a word nobody wrote is whatever the allocator last left there, and a verdict folded over it would admit peers nothing declared.

method.name: subtract
method.description: The bits in [param left] that [param right] does not have.

method.name: symmetric_difference
method.description: The bits exactly one of [param left] and [param right] has.

method.name: test
method.description: Whether [param row] has [param bit] set. A bit past the end of the row is not set rather than an error.

method.name: union_of
method.description: The bits either [param left] or [param right] has.

method.name: with_bit
method.description: A copy of [param row] with [param bit] set to [param value], widened if it did not reach that far.

method.name: word_count
method.description: How many words [param bit_count] bits need.

constants.constant: Usable bits per word. One short of 64, because the sign bit is left alone.
Every usable bit of one word.
